title: docs(error-catalog): INVALID_FIELD names the refusal of a search over an empty resolved search set
body:
Fixes #24331

Clause-②: no

## What

One sentence is added to the **Cause** text of `### INVALID_FIELD` in `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`, right after the `internal: true` sentence. It names the refusal that PR #24320 (`ec749fbb44`) added. When an object's resolved search set is empty, a non-blank `search` gets `400 INVALID_FIELD` with `param: 'search'`. It no longer gets every row back. The sentence also gives the two remedies the refusal message itself prescribes. No other entry changes and no section is added. The diff is +4 / -0 lines, all inside that entry.

## Read from the code, not from the card

The wording comes from the producer as it stands on the base `33f700b87b`. No commit between `ec749fbb44` and the base touches `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` or `packages/objectql/src/search-filter.ts`: the `git log` over that range and those paths is empty. `git merge-base --is-ancestor ec749fbb44 33f700b87b` exits 0.

- **Where.** `ObjectQL.expandSearchOnAst` in `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`. When `expandSearchToFilter` returns `null` and the normalized term is non-blank, it throws `emptySearchSetError(...)`. `find`, `findOne`, `count` and `aggregate` all reach this call.
- **Envelope.** `status: 400`, `code: 'INVALID_FIELD'`, `object`, `param: 'search'`. This matches the card.
- **When the set is empty.** `resolveSearchFieldResolution` in `packages/spec/src/data/search-fields.ts` runs over the object's fields after the `internal: true` ones are removed. A `searchableFields` entry counts only when it names an existing field that is not a `formula`. If no entry does, the auto-default is used, and the refusal fires only when the auto-default is empty too. The auto-default skips hidden fields, the system names in `SEARCH_AUTO_EXCLUDED_FIELDS` (`id`, `created_at`, `owner_id`, and others), and every type outside the textual set plus `select`.
- **Where the code differs from the card.** The card says the set is empty when "the object has no textual or enum stored field and no `searchableFields` entry naming one". The code differs in two ways. Some textual fields do not count: a hidden one, a system-named one, or one marked `internal: true`. And a declared entry may name any stored field, such as a `lookup` or `json` column, not only a textual one. So the sentence says "the default search scans none" and "`internal: true` fields never count", not "no textual or enum stored field".
- **Remedy.** The message ends with the two remedies: declare `searchableFields` on the object naming a stored field, or mirror the composed title onto a stored text field and search that. The card's remedies match the message. The sentence keeps both. It says "a composed title" because the catalog sets up no junction object for "the" to refer to.

## Acceptance notes

These other hand-written pages describe how `search` behaves on the data read route, and none of them mentions this refusal. They are left unchanged here because they are outside this card's file surface:

- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/error-handling.mdx:626`: says the catalog's `INVALID_FIELD` entry "enumerates every read axis this one code answers on". Its list in parentheses names `select`, `expand`, `searchFields`, `groupBy` and `aggregations[].field`, but not `search`.
- `content/docs/api/data-api.mdx:26`: the `search` parameter row. Also `content/docs/api/data-api.mdx:153-158`: a table of `search` / `searchFields` requests and their results, with no row for a bare `?search=` on an object that has no searchable field.
- `content/docs/data-modeling/queries.mdx:476` (the Full-Text Search section) and `content/docs/protocol/objectql/query-syntax.mdx:1120`: both describe how search fields are resolved and how `searchFields` is refused, but not this refusal.
